title: Operating rhythm & blockers catalog — Q3 synthesis (draft)
content:
Purpose
To synthesize the operating rhythm inputs from FY24 H1, enumerate persistent blockers across engineering/product/gtm, and propose a pragmatic all-hands + exec update framing that aligns teams around a focused Q3 set of priorities. This is a working doc — please add raw notes, links, and flagged asks under your name.

TL;DR / executive summary
- We're proposing 3 company-level objectives for Q3 (efficiency, reliability, customer momentum) with 6 KRs that are intentionally tight and measurable.
- The all-hands will be structured as a 45m sync + 15m breakout cadence: top-line metrics (10m) -> 3 objective deep dives (25m) -> customer spotlight + ask (10m) -> live Q&A (15m)
- Major cross-org blockers: model-onboarding velocity, SLA automation gaps for Dedicated, and incomplete rollout playbook for Private (network + KMS). Each blocker has a proposed owner and a 6-week mitigation plan.

Proposed Company OKRs (draft — for exec feedback)
Objective A: Reduce per-token inference cost while preserving response quality
- KR A1: 20% reduction in average hosted token cost (baseline: May 2024)
- KR A2: Deploy two quantized model profiles covering 60% of production traffic with <1% quality regression on core evals

Objective B: Make inference predictable at scale (latency & availability)
- KR B1: 99.95% p99 availability for Redwood API across US/EU regions for top 10 routes
- KR B2: Reduce p95 latency on typical conversational workload by 15% via batching/compilation optimizations

Objective C: Drive enterprise adoption for Private & Dedicated
- KR C1: Convert 3 pilot customers to contracts (>=12mo) for Dedicated or Private deployments
- KR C2: Ship the Private deployment hardening checklist and complete one on-prem pilot with KMS integration

All-hands run of show (proposed: 60 minutes)
- 00:00–00:05 Welcome / theme (CEO) — why Q3 matters; framing ask: focus on predictable economics
- 00:05–00:15 Metrics lightning (Head of Eng) — MRR trends, latency trends (p50/p95/p99), hosting cost per 1M tokens
- 00:15–00:30 OKR deep dives (3 owners, 5min each + 5min consolidated questions)
  - Efficiency / Optimize (Product + Applied ML)
  - Reliability / Serving Runtime (SRE + Serving Runtime)
  - GTM / Private + Dedicated ramp (Sales + Solutions Engineering)
- 00:30–00:40 Customer spotlight (Customer Success) — short case: pilot outcomes + concrete asks for eng
- 00:40–00:55 Live Q&A (moderated via #allhands-questions)
- 00:55–01:00 Closing — ops cadence & follow-ups (People Ops)

Decision points for Execs (need before slides finalized on 7/30)
- Approve the three-objective structure and final OKR wording
- Set the target for hosted token-cost reduction (A1) — is 20% acceptable or too aggressive?
- Confirm the sales threshold for auto-escalation to enterprise support for Dedicated pilots (C1)

Blockers catalog (high-priority items, owners, proposed 6-week plan)
- Blocker 1: Model onboarding velocity (Owner: Miguel Alvarez)
  - Symptom: average time from model candidate -> production profile = 7 weeks (too slow); manual kernel tuning + missing test harnesses
  - 6-week plan: dedicate a 1-week kernel selection spike; create a baseline test harness; automate CI quantization smoke tests
  - Dependencies: infra quota, test data access (Data Platform)

- Blocker 2: SLA automation gaps for Dedicated (Owner: Hannah Lee)
  - Symptom: manual checks for capacity and scale; on-call runbooks not integrated with console alerts
  - 6-week plan: implement auto-alerts for capacity thresholds; ship runbook templates in Console; one rehearsal incident drill
  - Dependencies: observability team (Traces & Metrics), runbook storage

- Blocker 3: Private deployment rollout playbook incomplete (Owner: Tom Becker)
  - Symptom: network and KMS integration steps not standardized; customer-facing docs missing
  - 6-week plan: finalize checklist, create a customer onboarding template, and run 1 internal dry-run with Solutions Eng
  - Risks: legal review of KMS patterns may add 2–3 weeks

Risks + mitigations (short list)
- Risk: Quality regressions with aggressive quantization -> Mitigation: gated rollouts + eval set-specific thresholds + automatic rollback
- Risk: Sales churn if Dedicated latency targets slip -> Mitigation: canary SLAs and explicit communication template (customer success)
- Risk: All-hands perceived as tactical update rather than strategy session -> Mitigation: clear theme communicated in pre-reads + CEO framing + 2 strategic anecdotes

Preparation checklist (owners + deadlines) — finalize by 2024-07-30
- Slide deck skeleton (Priya) — 7/24
- Top-line metric pulls: billing, latency, usage patterns (Data Platform) — 7/22
- OKR copy finalization (Exec team) — 7/25
- Customer spotlight prep + permission to name (CS) — 7/26
- Q&A backlog assembled from #allhands-questions (People Ops) — ongoing

Post all-hands follow-ups (30/60/90 day)
- 30d: publish prioritized blocker sprint board + owners (company-ops)
- 60d: measure intermediate KR deltas and publish heatmap (Product + Eng)
- 90d: executive readout and Q4 draft alignment session

Notes to self / rough fragments (please keep adding raw items below)
- Consider a quick poll during the all-hands about preferred cadence for tech deep dives (monthly vs quarterly)
- Add a short customer quote slide — 1 line + screenshot if permitted
- Ops: think through backup plan if keynote presenter is delayed (pre-recorded 5m segment)

Open questions (flagged for exec discussion)
- Should we make cost reduction (A1) measured against a usage-normalized baseline (recommended) or absolute dollars?
- Any objections to the proposed all-hands length (60m)? Some teams prefer 90m for more discussion.

Action items (immediate)
- Priya: lock room + calendar invite + pre-read distribution (7/22)
- Miguel: deliver model onboarding spike plan (7/24)
- Hannah: list of current Dedicated incidents and latency postmortems to use as examples (7/24)
- Tom: draft Private deployment checklist + two-step signoff (7/26)

If you add items, please tag using the format: "[NAME] — short note".

Related links & references
- Confluence: Operating Rhythm Home (linked above)
- Jira: OPS-4321 (blocker tracker)
- Roadmap PR: github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/78

End of draft — please add edits in-line or leave comments.

- Priya
